## Motivation

This PR optimizes the JIT `fused_qknorm_rope` kernel.

`fused_qknorm_rope` fuses Q/K RMSNorm and RoPE application into a single kernel. The baseline JIT implementation had several inefficiencies in the hot loop, especially for interleaved / GPT-J style RoPE:

- Scalar RMSNorm weight loads
- Extra intermediate register arrays

`fused_kda_conv_gating_verify` rolled the conv state back into `conv_state` at the end of the kernel. Every V tile loads that same Q/K conv history at entry, but only `i_v == 0` writes it, so a tile scheduled in a later wave reads what the owner already overwrote.

The change is expanding WAR fences to prefill support based on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31686/changes by @hnyls2002.

The overlap scheduler can prepare the next batch while the previous forward is still running on another CUDA stream. Before it rewrites shared request and attention metadata, the WAR barrier must wait for the previous forward's final read of that state.
The existing decode path can publish only before or after an entire CUDA graph replay, so it cannot express a read boundary inside the graph. NVIDIA recently open-sourced [SANA-WM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15178), a 2.6B Text+Image-to-Video (TI2V) world model that generates 720p video from a text prompt, a first-frame image, and an optional 6-DoF camera trajectory.
